facts.text: The hotel is in the former First National Bank Tower, which has anchored Dallas's Main Street District since 1965.
facts.excerpt: Since 1965, the First National Bank Tower has anchored the Main Street District with a modern, global vision of Dallas.

facts.text: The building's exterior was designed in the 1960s by architect George Dahl.
facts.excerpt: The exterior was designed in the ‘60s by George Dahl, the architect behind some of Dallas’s most iconic buildings, including much of Fair Park and the Neimans flagship.

facts.text: The National was once the tallest building west of the Mississippi.
facts.excerpt: Once the tallest building west of the Mississippi, the National sat vacant for nearly a decade before developers launched a complete renovation.

facts.text: Thompson Dallas is the first Thompson hotel in Texas and takes up about half the building, with offices and residences on the upper floors.
facts.excerpt: The first Thompson outpost in Texas now takes up about half the building, with office spaces and residences on the upper floors.

facts.text: Original materials such as the ninth floor's travertine walls were restored.
facts.excerpt: much of the building’s original materials, like the ninth floor’s travertine walls, were restored.

facts.text: The National also houses Samuel Lynne Galleries, showing contemporary art, and Lucchese, known for handcrafted Western style.
facts.excerpt: Thompson Dallas calls The National home alongside Samuel Lynne Galleries, showcasing contemporary art, and Lucchese, carrying forward a legacy of handcrafted Western style.

facts.text: Rooms are designed with mid-century flair, walnut woods and brass touches.

facts.text: Room decor brings in 1960s-style furniture, light fixtures and brass accents, styled with cow print and leather.
facts.excerpt: Mad Men–meets–urban–cowboy decor brings in 1960s-style furniture, light fixtures, and brass accents, all styled with cow print and leather.
